messages:
Maria Chen: heads up — invoice-preview for tenant acme-inc shows a weird +12k credit bump after the backfill finished. looks like route-penalty was applied twice for the same sessions.
Ajay Patel: can you paste the preview diff or the events?
Maria Chen: pasted a minimal example below. notice same session_id with two penalty records, different processing_stage tags.
Maria Chen: ```
event_id: evt_0x9a
session_id: sess_123
tenant: acme-inc
charge_unit: token
amount: 0.02
penalty_tag: route-penalty
processing_stage: initial-enrich
---
event_id: evt_0x9a
session_id: sess_123
tenant: acme-inc
charge_unit: token
amount: 0.02
penalty_tag: route-penalty
processing_stage: backfill-aggregate
```
Kevin O'Neill: billing-backfill job emits a synthetic event during aggregation to reconstruct missing penalties. looks like it didn't detect the earlier penalty because canonical_fingerprint changed (edge proxy header normalization).
Lina Gomez: yup — I saw fingerprint churn for that client. proxy used to include `x-client-hint` which we drop in enrich; backfill used raw payload so fingerprint != canonical.
billing-bot: Billing backfill completed window=2026-03-21T00:00Z status=success rows_written=12456.
Ajay Patel: root cause: backfill path lacked idempotence key (we use `origin_event_id` when present). if fingerprint differs we can't match. quick fix is to derive canonical_fingerprint in backfill the same way as runtime enrich and use `origin_event_id` as dedupe key.
Maria Chen: will that avoid double-charges in invoice-preview?
Kevin O'Neill: preview will reflect changes after a re-run, but downstream invoices already derived from that aggregate stream might still show the bump until we reprocess affected windows. we should avoid reprocessing global history until we have dedupe guarantee.
Lina Gomez: short term: patch backfill to compute canonical_fingerprint and skip emitting penalty if an event with same origin_event_id/fingerprint already in processed ledger. patch proposal: 
```sql
-- pseudo
INSERT INTO penalties (event_id, fingerprint, amount, stage)
SELECT e.id, canonical_fingerprint(e), e.amount, 'backfill'
FROM backfill_events e
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM penalties p WHERE p.origin_event_id = e.origin_event_id OR p.fingerprint = canonical_fingerprint(e));
```
Ajay Patel: I'll open a tiny PR to add the fingerprint normalization helper and the `WHERE NOT EXISTS` guard. will target canary backfill runner first.
Product Ops: if invoices already went out to customers we may need to issue manual credits — @Maria can you generate a list of affected tenants by query?
Maria Chen: on it, running query now. will upload to shared drive and flag CS for acme-inc.
sre-oncall: tagging this for the next canary deploy window. @Ajay please include a migration to mark reprocessed windows in replay log so we can reason about re-runs.
Ajay Patel: noted — will add migration marker and an idempotence flag to the backfill job metadata.
Kevin O'Neill: also add a dashboard panel in console: "backfill dedupe hits" (count of skipped duplicates) and a grafana alert if duplicates > threshold in a run. saves us a repeat.
Lina Gomez: agree. I'll add a telemetry event `billing.backfill.dedupe_skipped` with `tenant` and `window` tags.
Maria Chen: thx. next steps: Ajay PR, canary run, generate affected-tenant list, product decision on manual credits.
Ajay Patel: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/backfill/+/42 (draft) — includes fingerprint normalization + dedupe guard. will request reviews.
Product Ops: thanks. I'll prepare CS playbook for crediting if invoice confirms mismatch after re-run.
Maria Chen: marking this resolved for now. follow-ups: reopen if preview still shows dupes after canary. :thumbsup:
Kevin O'Neill: :eyes: good catch Maria.
billing-bot: Incident note created: BILLBACK-2026-031.
